messages.text:
Cuenta regresiva para el halving de Nexa: 3 días

La prueba de trabajo (PoW) y la oferta monetaria predecible son fundamentales para que las criptomonedas funcionen como dinero, pero la mayoría de las criptomonedas PoW carecen de velocidad y funcionalidad.

Por otro lado, en el caso de la prueba de participación (Proof-of-Stake) y las EVM, su modelo Turing-completo carece de determinismo y genera firmas ciegas, MEV y otros problemas que perjudican a los usuarios.

Nexa está creando la primera blockchain híbrida tradicional y de grafo acíclico dirigido (DAG) con subbloques, acelerándola con hardware e integrando firmas post-cuánticas, todo ello sobre un modelo UTXO determinista.

Sigue la cuenta regresiva para el halving de Nexa 👇
https://halving.nexa.org/
messages.translation:
Countdown to the Nexa halving: 3 days

Proof-of-work (PoW) and a predictable monetary supply are fundamental for cryptocurrencies to work as money, but most PoW cryptocurrencies lack speed and functionality.

On the other hand, in the case of Proof-of-Stake and EVMs, their Turing-complete model lacks determinism and produces blind signing, MEV and other problems that harm users.

Nexa is building the first hybrid traditional and directed acyclic graph (DAG) blockchain with subblocks, accelerating it with hardware and integrating post-quantum signatures, all on top of a deterministic UTXO model.

Follow the countdown to the Nexa halving 👇
https://halving.nexa.org/

Cuenta regresiva para el halving de Nexa: 2 días

El primer y más importante halving de Nexa se acerca en menos de 48 horas. El próximo halving tendrá lugar aproximadamente en 4 años, alrededor de 2030.

El suministro total de Nexa está diseñado para reducirse gradualmente mediante ciclos de halving durante más de 100 años. El objetivo final es lograr y mantener las recompensas de minería únicamente a partir de las comisiones por transacción.

Es el mismo modelo que el de Bitcoin. Sin embargo, en el caso de Nexa, es mucho más factible debido a su alto rendimiento de transacciones, programabilidad y tamaño.

Las aplicaciones descentralizadas, los exchanges y otras aplicaciones en la cadena de bloques, como juegos, mercados de predicción, etc., pueden contribuir drásticamente a un ecosistema autónomo y sostenible en un modelo de prueba de trabajo.

Sigue la cuenta regresiva del halving: https://halving.nexa.org
messages.translation:
Countdown to the Nexa halving: 2 days

Nexa's first and most important halving is coming in less than 48 hours. The next halving will take place in about 4 years, around 2030.

Nexa's total supply is designed to be gradually reduced through halving cycles over more than 100 years. The ultimate goal is to achieve and sustain mining rewards solely from transaction fees.

It's the same model as Bitcoin's. However, in Nexa's case it's far more feasible due to its high transaction throughput, programmability and size.

Decentralized applications, exchanges and other on-chain applications, such as games, prediction markets, etc., can contribute dramatically to an autonomous and sustainable ecosystem under a proof-of-work model.

Follow the halving countdown: https://halving.nexa.org

Nueva versión: NexScript v1.1.0

Nos complace presentarles la nueva versión de NexScript v.1.1.0. Esta es una versión importante que optimiza la programación de Nexa en el backend.

Se ha trabajado intensamente para que sea más limpia y confiable, integrándola con la mayor parte del ecosistema Nexa. Las interacciones en la cadena ahora están consolidadas y alineadas con la biblioteca TypeScript de Nexa.

Para los desarrolladores, hay un cambio que merece su atención. Ahora, NexScript utiliza por defecto una prueba de registro local en lugar de conectarse a una red en vivo. Todos los proveedores de red ahora deben especificar un tipo de entorno.

Para una revisión más detallada, visite el foro de Nexa en el enlace a continuación.

https://forum.nexa.org/t/new-release-nexscript-v1-1-0/1691
messages.translation:
New release: NexScript v1.1.0

We're pleased to present the new release of NexScript v.1.1.0. This is an important release that optimizes Nexa programming on the backend.

A lot of work has gone into making it cleaner and more reliable, integrating it with most of the Nexa ecosystem. On-chain interactions are now consolidated and aligned with Nexa's TypeScript library.

For developers, there's one change that deserves your attention. NexScript now defaults to a local regtest instead of connecting to a live network. All network providers must now specify an environment type.

For a more detailed review, visit the Nexa forum at the link below.

https://forum.nexa.org/t/new-release-nexscript-v1-1-0/1691
messages.note: "prueba de registro local" is a translation of "local regtest", the regression-test network mode.

Nueva versión: LibNexaKotlin 0.5.66

El equipo de Nexa se complace en anunciar LibNexaKotlin 0.5.66, que incluye importantes correcciones y mejoras para la biblioteca Nexa Kotlin. Recientemente se han publicado varias actualizaciones, y se recomienda a todos los desarrolladores que utilizan la biblioteca que actualicen a la última versión.

LibNexaKotlin es un completo conjunto de herramientas multiplataforma para la blockchain de Nexa, compatible con Android, iOS, JVM y múltiples plataformas nativas de escritorio. Permite a los desarrolladores crear monederos, acceder a los datos de la blockchain e interactuar con contratos inteligentes. La mejor manera de aprender a usar la biblioteca es mediante el código de ejemplo, con la documentación como referencia.

El desarrollo de esta biblioteca central de la infraestructura de monederos de Nexa continúa activamente, y se planean más actualizaciones en las próximas semanas y meses.

Los desarrolladores principales del equipo de Nexa están integrando Tailstorm, un diseño basado en grafos acíclicos dirigidos (DAG) de bloques, derivado de la investigación de Tailstorm. El modelo Tailstorm representa una importante evolución arquitectónica, pasando de una cadena de bloques lineal a un DAG de subbloques, a la vez que conserva una cadena convencional de "bloques resumen". La fusión del modelo de bloques resumen con la cadena tradicional permite a Nexa aprovechar ambos enfoques, adoptando mecanismos más avanzados de minería y propagación de bloques.

messages.translation:
Nexa's core developers are integrating Tailstorm, a block-DAG (directed acyclic graph) based design derived from the Tailstorm research. The Tailstorm model represents a major architectural evolution, moving from a linear blockchain to a sub-block DAG, while retaining a conventional chain of "summary blocks". Merging the summary block model with the traditional chain lets Nexa take advantage of both approaches, adopting more advanced mining and block propagation mechanisms.

Nexa Jar: Explicación de la tokenómica

La mayoría ya conoce este modelo, pero no todos saben que el Nexa Jar es el mismo que el de Bitcoin.

¿Te has preguntado alguna vez por qué 21 billones y no 21 millones? Porque la coma decimal se movió seis posiciones, convirtiendo lo que serían fracciones de una moneda en unidades completas.

El número total de satoshis es exactamente el mismo que el de Bitcoin: 2,1 cuatrillones. Nexa simplemente usa dos decimales en lugar de ocho, lo cual es mucho más práctico para el uso diario, de la misma manera que manejamos las monedas fiduciarias.

21 billones de NEXA es el suministro máximo, y por consenso, no se minará por completo hasta 2138.

Cada 1.050.000 bloques, aproximadamente cada cuatro años, la recompensa por minería se reduce a la mitad.

El primer halving de Nexa tuvo lugar el 1 de mayo de 2026, cuando la recompensa por bloque se redujo de 10 000 000 a 5 000 000 NEXA.

messages.translation:
Nexa Jar: Tokenomics explained

Most people already know this model, but not everyone knows that the Nexa Jar is the same as Bitcoin's.

Have you ever wondered why 21 trillion and not 21 million? Because the decimal point was moved six places, turning what would be fractions of a coin into whole units.

The total number of satoshis is exactly the same as Bitcoin's: 2.1 quadrillion. Nexa simply uses two decimals instead of eight, which is far more practical for everyday use, in the same way we handle fiat currencies.

21 trillion NEXA is the maximum supply, and by consensus, it won't be fully mined until 2138.

Every 1,050,000 blocks, roughly every four years, the mining reward is cut in half.

Nexa's first halving took place on May 1, 2026, when the block reward dropped from 10,000,000 to 5,000,000 NEXA.

https://emission.nexa.org
messages.note: 'Nexa Jar' refers to the coin-supply 'jar' visualization of tokenomics.

messages.text:
Lo que satoshi hizo fue dejar 8 decimales solo por si a caso en un futuro se necesitaba. Pero su intención no era mostrar todos los decimales, sino solo los que tuviera sentido mostrar. Su intencion como dejó por escrito en los foros era mover la coma cuando se necesitara para adaptar el precio de los bitcoins a un valor razonable para ser moneda. No entiendo por qué todo el mundo ignoró eso, incluso nexa,  y aún seguimos mostrando en todos lados 8 decimales, o en el mejor de los casos, mover directamente la coma en la posición de la última etapa planificada (después se podría seguir agregando subsatoshis etc).

La propuesta era:
Mientras un Bitcoin tenga un valor razonable para una moneda, mantener 1 Bitcoin= 100 millones de sats.
Si bitcoin hacia un x100 o x1000 y se estabilizaba, simplemente hacer que 1 bitcoin = 1 millón de sats etc, eso es algo que ya debería haber pasado y que cada vez tardaría mas decadas e incluso generaciones en volver a pasar.

Entonces la gente para prácticamente todas las transacciones habrian hablado siempre de precios de entre 0,01 y 10000 bitcoins, nunca 0,00053747 (caso BTC actual) o 4838294328 (caso nexa actual) para un gasto común.
messages.translation:
What Satoshi did was leave 8 decimals just in case they were needed in the future. But his intention wasn't to display all the decimals, only the ones that made sense to display. His intention, as he put in writing on the forums, was to move the decimal point when needed to adapt the price of bitcoins to a reasonable value for it to be a currency. I don't understand why everybody ignored that, including Nexa, and we're still showing 8 decimals everywhere, or in the best case, just moving the point straight to the position of the last planned stage (afterwards you could keep adding sub-satoshis, etc.).

The proposal was:
As long as a Bitcoin has a reasonable value for a currency, keep 1 Bitcoin = 100 million sats.
If bitcoin did a x100 or x1000 and stabilized, simply make 1 bitcoin = 1 million sats, etc. That's something that should have happened already and that each time would take more decades, even generations, to happen again.

That way people would have talked about prices between 0.01 and 10000 bitcoins for practically every transaction, never 0.00053747 (the current BTC case) or 4838294328 (the current Nexa case) for an ordinary expense.

messages.text: Como creador de una plataforma social donde las transacciones p2p son parte de la experiencia natural me parece una fricción absurda que los usuarios tengan que lidiar con ese tipo de numeros tan antiintuitivos. Lástima que se puso tanto el foco en la especulación, porque si nos hubieramos centrado en quitar fricciones para USAR la moneda, mantener el valor dentro de un rango razonable para una moneda con simplemente desplazar la coma cuando se necesite e ignorando los decimales carentes de valor, era una de las propuestas mas básicas que no se habrían olvidado.
messages.translation: As the creator of a social platform where p2p transactions are part of the natural experience, it seems to me an absurd friction that users have to deal with that kind of counterintuitive numbers. Too bad so much focus was put on speculation, because if we had focused on removing friction to USE the currency, keeping the value within a reasonable range for a currency by simply shifting the decimal point when needed and ignoring the worthless decimals, that was one of the most basic proposals that wouldn't have been forgotten.

messages.text:
Aceleración por hardware: escalabilidad mediante circuitos

En el segundo artículo de esta serie, construimos el motor de validación de Nexa a partir de seis componentes, una cinta y un cabezal, y observamos cómo procesaba un pago de Alice a Bob sin ejecutar ningún software.

Dado que la cinta solo se desplazaba en sentido directo, el motor cumplió con el primero de los cuatro requisitos que debe satisfacer un Bitcoin mejorado: la capacidad de procesamiento en tubería (*pipelining*).

Este artículo aborda los requisitos restantes. Tal como demostró en Sídney el Dr. Peter Rizun (@PeterRizun), científico jefe de Nexa, es posible perfeccionar el Bitcoin de Satoshi y lograr que cumpla todas esas condiciones con solo tres cambios sencillos; de paso, el motor adquiere dos propiedades adicionales —extensibilidad y compresibilidad— prácticamente sin coste alguno.

https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749
messages.translation:
Hardware acceleration: scaling by circuit

In the second article of this series, we built Nexa's validation engine out of six components, a tape and a head, and watched it process a payment from Alice to Bob without running any software.

Since the tape only moved forward, the engine met the first of the four requirements an improved Bitcoin must satisfy: pipelining.

This article tackles the remaining requirements. As Dr. Peter Rizun (@PeterRizun), Nexa's chief scientist, demonstrated in Sydney, it's possible to refine Satoshi's Bitcoin and make it meet all those conditions with just three simple changes; along the way, the engine gains two additional properties — extensibility and compressibility — at practically no cost.

summary.headline: Near-pure announcement feed: Nexa's first halving, NexScript/wallet releases, Tailstorm and hardware work, with rare member questions.
summary.summary: This window of the Spanish-language Nexa group is dominated by Blacktea ▽, who posts translated official announcements almost daily, with very little back-and-forth from members. The first arc is the countdown to Nexa's first halving (May 1, 2026), the Halving Fest 2026 NFT art contest on NiftyArt, and the 'New Baseline' X Spaces. From May onward the feed shifts to development news: NexScript v1.1.0 and Playground upgrades, LibNexaKotlin and Wally Wallet releases, an updated Explorer with HODL Vaults, the 2026-27 roadmap, Nexa's 4th anniversary Spaces with Andrew Stone, and heavy coverage of Tailstorm plus Peter Rizun's Blitz hardware and the NexaPoW 2.0 / cellular automaton mining redesign, culminating in Full-Node 2.2.0.0 as the last release before the Tailstorm hard fork. Member participation is sparse but concrete: JAPM13 asks for news (and later about staking), Josep Forexsand asks whether the node update affects mining and where Europeans can trade NEXA, Manel recommends nonkyc.io, and Satori posts a two-message critique of Nexa's decimal/unit design. Warning notes about Exbitron and BitMart shutting down are the only clearly negative items.

topics.title: First halving countdown and Halving Fest
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ ran a daily countdown to the May 1, 2026 halving (block 1,050,000, reward cut from 10M to 5M NEXA), promoted the Halving Fest 2026 NFT art contest on NiftyArt with a $250 prize, and announced the 'New Baseline' X Spaces and the halving recap.

topics.title: Tailstorm, NexaPoW 2.0 and hardware
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ posted extensively on the Tailstorm block-DAG integration ahead of the second hard fork, Peter Rizun's Blitz FPGA hardware node ('A Node Made of Wires', 'Scaling by Circuit'), and the NexaPoW 2.0 cellular-automaton algorithm intended to make mining ASIC-resistant and FPGA-only.

topics.title: Dev releases: NexScript, wallets, explorer
topics.summary: Announcements covered NexScript v1.1.0 (now defaulting to local regtest) and Playground upgrades, LibNexaKotlin 0.5.66/0.5.68, Wally Wallet 3.30 beta and 3.30.02 patch with peer-to-peer swaps, and Nexa Explorer additions including HODL Vaults and self-hosting.

topics.title: Full-Node 2.2.0.0 and mining question
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ urged everyone to update to Full-Node 2.2.0.0, the last release before the Tailstorm hard fork, adding rolling checkpoints at 200 confirmations; Josep Forexsand asked if it affects mining and Blacktea ▽ said not yet, only after the hard fork, while Manel thanked the team.

topics.title: 4th anniversary, webinars and newsletters
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ announced and recapped the June 21 anniversary X Spaces with Andrew Stone, Andrea Suisani and David Thibodeau (plus commemorative NFTs), EvolvH3R webinars with David Thibodeau, Steven van den Meiracker (the 'Nexa Warriors' on-chain card game) and Andrew Clifford, along with monthly newsletters, the emission schedule site and the 2026-27 roadmap.

topics.title: Exchanges, delistings and where to buy
topics.summary: Blacktea ▽ flagged Exbitron's permanent shutdown and BitMart's imminent closure; Josep Forexsand asked about a Europe-authorized exchange for NEXA trading after being burned by frozen funds on CoinEx, and Manel recommended nonkyc.io, while the Rose bot listed the usual exchanges with a self-custody warning.

topics.title: Debate on units and decimals
topics.summary: Satori argued, replying to the 'Nexa Jar' tokenomics post, that Satoshi intended the decimal point to be shifted as value grew and that Nexa (like Bitcoin) ignored this, leaving users with unintuitive numbers like 4,838,294,328 NEXA for ordinary payments — friction he finds absurd as the creator of a p2p social platform.

topics.title: Member questions and quiet channel
topics.summary: JAPM13 asked whether there was news since the English channel seemed more active — Blacktea ▽ replied weeks later that he had started translating all official announcements — and later asked whether NEXA can be staked or put to work; that last question was still unanswered at the end of the window.

summary.mood_description: The tone is consistently optimistic but almost entirely one-directional: Blacktea ▽ broadcasts polished announcements and the group rarely responds. Genuine excitement peaks around the halving and the anniversary Spaces, and the Tailstorm/hardware posts read as confident momentum. The few human exchanges add mild friction — worry about exchanges shutting down or freezing funds, Satori's criticism of unintuitive unit denominations, and unanswered questions about staking — but nothing escalates into conflict.

highlights.why: The actual halving moment: supply crossed 50% and block rewards dropped from 10M to 5M NEXA.
The only substantive community critique in the window — Satori argues Nexa (and Bitcoin) ignored Satoshi's intent to shift the decimal point, leaving unusable numbers.
Operationally important: Full-Node 2.2.0.0 is the last release before the Tailstorm hard fork, with a call to update and back up wallet.dat.
Explains the planned NexaPoW 2.0 cellular automaton that would make mining ASIC-resistant and FPGA-only — a major change for miners.
Blacktea ▽ answering a three-week-old question about the channel being quiet by saying he's started translating all official announcements — the reason this feed exists.
